newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: European Leisure says dividend likely in "97.
newsitem.headline: European Leisure says dividend likely in "97.

text.p: European Leisure Plc said on Tuesday that it expects to pay a dividend on its ordinary shares for the financial year ending June 30, 1997.

Chairman Clive Bastin told the annual meeting that provided the proposals in a recent circular sent to shareholders were implemented, and in the absence of unforeseen circumstances, it anticipated paying a dividend.
Earlier this month, European Leisure announced a two-for-three rights issue at 145 pence per share to raise 11.4 million sterling net of expenses.
The proceeds of the issue, which is fully underwritten by Charterhouse Bank Ltd, will be used primarily to fund a focused expansion programme, European Leisure said in a statement.
The company also announced the early conversion of preference shares owned by its banking syndicate into new ordinary shares which will be placed with institutional investors at 145 pence per share.
A further 1.8 million shares owned by members of the banking syndicate will also be placed taking the gross value of the placing to 20.3 million sterling.
Bastin said the resolutions had been passed at the extraordinary general meeting held on Tuesday.
He said turnover in the various sectors of the business were ahead of or at the same level as last year.
"We are pleased that the company is now back on a firm footing with a prudently funded and focused development strategy," Bastin said.
